rounds.rationale: pick_place@0.2.1 targets the most common gate failure, grasp_slip (27/100); the ik_failures (23/100) almost all came after a slip, grasp_miss and regrasp. The main change: the ball is carried 3 cm above the place height instead of v0.2.0's 10 cm hover. Slips cluster on low-friction seeds and got worse when I slowed the carry, which suggests the held ball creeps out of the soft finger contacts over time, so a shorter lift and path (the goal region has no walls) loses it far less often. A smaller change: the grip now keeps closing for at least 8 steps and until the measured width stops changing, rather than a fixed 4 steps that was shorter than the up-to-5-step action latency; on its own this took dev from 53% to 60%. Dev success went from 16/30 (53%) with v0.2.0 to 29/30 (97%), and 96/100 on 100 dev seeds; ideas that did not help (smoothed carry, a 90-degree pre-squeeze, averaged observations, a lower grasp height) were removed.

rounds.rationale:
pick_place@0.2.2 targets grasp_slip (10/100 gate failures), which in every case ended with a failed re-grasp: the re-grasp descended toward a noisy, low-pass-filtered position and, after a slip, toward a ball that was still rolling (debug logs showed misses 4–18 cm off).
It adds a localize step at the pre-grasp hover that waits until a least-squares velocity fit over the last 12 raw observations shows the ball at rest, then descends to their outlier-trimmed mean, switching back to tracking the ball if it moves more than 1.5 cm; it also squeezes for at least 20 steps instead of 8 before lifting, which cut first-attempt slips/misses on 100 dev seeds from 14 to 10.
Dev success on 100 seeds went from 96/100 (0.2.1) to 97/100 (2 grasp_slip, 1 ik_failure), and 30-seed dev from 29/30 to 30/30; that gain is within noise, so the gate's paired test should decide.
Things I tried and dropped because they measured worse on dev: a speed/acceleration-limited carry (91/100, more ik_failures), changing grasp height (92–95/100, no change in slips), and waiting for the ball to stop before every re-plan plus more miss retries (92–94/100, the waits use up the 300-step budget).

rounds.rationale: pick_place@0.2.2 targets grasp_slip, the most common gate failure of 0.2.1 (10/100). Those slips cluster on low-friction, high-gain or heavy-ball seeds within about 100 steps of the grasp, so the ball is squeezed out by jerky acceleration during lift and transport, not by bad re-grasps. During lift and transport the arm now follows a waypoint that moves at most 2 cm per control step (0.4 m/s) in a straight line toward the goal; the waypoint is reset on every re-grasp attempt, and approach, descent and place are unchanged. A first version limited the target relative to the lagging EE; it stopped the slips but was too slow (70% dev, 7 timeouts), so I replaced it with a waypoint that advances on its own clock. Dev success after the change is 30/30 (100%), and 96/100 on 100 dev seeds (2 slips, 2 ik_failure, 1 collision); I could not re-run 0.2.1 on the dev seeds in this sandbox, so the "before" figure is its gate rate of 85%, not a dev measurement.

rounds.rationale:
pick_place@0.2.2 lengthens the grip settle before lifting: the fingers must close for at least 14 steps (was 8) and the measured width must hold steady for 6 steps (was 3) before the lift starts.
It targets grasp_slip, the most common gate failure of 0.2.1 (10/100). Those slips happen on seeds with high actuator gain, low friction and up to 5 steps of action latency, within about 85–110 steps of the grasp, which points to the lift starting before the squeeze has settled.
Dev success before: 85% (0.2.1 gate rate; I did not re-measure it on dev). Dev success after: NOT MEASURED, because Bash permission was denied and I could not run ./dev_eval.
Treat this change as untested until ./dev_eval confirms it raises the rate and causes no new timeouts.
